status: Concrete source-level measurement finding; journal novelty unresolved

findings.name: Namespace identity loss
findings.evidence: Creation timestamps keyed by netpol.Name; aggregation also keys by unqualified policy name. Fixture writes ns-one/allow at 100ms then ns-two/allow at 900ms. Observation for first at 200ms reports -700ms instead of 100ms.
findings.limit: Timestamp-map setup is mirrored from callback; aggregation loop is extracted unmodified. The supplied default template makes names iteration-specific and avoids this collision. No claim that default benchmark results exhibit it.

findings.name: Shared-flow attribution ambiguity
findings.evidence: One successful flow is reused for multiple policies. A flow at 300ms yields A=200ms and B=100ms with creation times 100/200ms. Changing B's unobserved realization time cannot change this output.
findings.limit: Valid as shared effective-connectivity measurement. It cannot independently establish each overlapping policy's realization. Additive policy semantics are already known; no novel theorem claimed.

findings.name: Negative interval inclusion
findings.evidence: B created at 400ms with shared success at 300ms contributes -100ms. Source warns and retains it.
findings.limit: Negative values are explicitly acknowledged in existing source. Their existence is not a new discovery.

version_check: The same name-only creation-map and shared-result loop strings were also present at 5131d57bb3315e29f4bcf896f09926a7dd71ccc0, the latest file-changing commit returned by the API during review. Only the older pinned loop was executed.

closest_work.assessment: PR explicitly documents deduplicating identical flow probes. Therefore deduplication is intentional, not an undiscovered implementation behavior.
Allow policies combine additively. A successful shared flow does not uniquely identify its enabling policy.
ATPG already addresses rule coverage and fault localization. Abstract and introduction reviewed here. Full algorithm comparison required before proposing unique-witness testing as new.
Test Coverage for Network Configurations is a relevant further baseline; abstract-level screening only.

search_scope: Targeted public web searches plus GitHub issue search for netpol latency and PR 671/679 descriptions/comments. No matching namespace report found in inspected results. This is not an exhaustive novelty search.
potential_research_question: How often do realistic benchmark policy sets permit per-policy latency identification, and how much do unsupported attribution and identity loss alter reported deadline outcomes?
publication_gate: Execute native callback/aggregation regression in full upstream package
Reproduce valid non-default same-name workload end to end
Quantify overlap in supplied workload templates
Show material consequences beyond a straightforward map-key bug
engineering_next: Separate namespaced object identity from flow identity; report shared reachability separately from uniquely evidenced policy realization. Keep a simple namespace-key correction as the strongest baseline.
external_reporting: No upstream issue, message or submission sent.
